metaDescription: Canonsburg mineral owners along Chartiers Creek: get a plain-English cash offer on your Marcellus royalty interest, no obligation.
heroLead: Canonsburg is bigger and more built up than most towns on this list, but plenty of the older family tracts around its edges still carry mineral rights nobody's fully sorted out.
intro: Canonsburg sits along Chartiers Creek in one of the more developed parts of Washington County, and while the town itself has grown well past its farming roots, the outlying tracts and older family parcels around it are squarely inside the county's Marcellus leasehold. If you own minerals connected to this area, there's a real chance the tract has been part of an active unit for years, quietly generating a royalty check you've never had explained in plain terms.
We've walked through that exact confusion with our own family's holdings, which is why we start every conversation by explaining what the paperwork says, not by pushing a number.

sections.heading: Development pressure and mineral value
paragraphs: As towns like Canonsburg grow, surface development can complicate future drilling on specific parcels even while the underlying mineral rights remain fully valid and, in many cases, still tied to production from nearby units. Owners sometimes assume growth near their tract means their minerals are somehow less relevant; usually the opposite is true, since existing units keep producing regardless of what's built on the surface miles away.
This part of the county is in the wet-gas Marcellus fairway, with Range Resources and CNX among the operators holding significant leasehold in the surrounding townships.

sections.heading: Reading the fine print on an older lease
paragraphs: Leases signed in this area during the early Marcellus years often used different royalty and deduction language than what's standard today. We review the actual lease language tied to your interest, not a generic assumption, before explaining what your royalty statement is showing you.

sections.heading: What clean title looks like here
paragraphs: We confirm your chain of title through the Washington County Recorder of Deeds and check for any gaps, unresolved estates, or unrecorded transfers before finalizing an offer, so there are no surprises at closing.

faqs.question: Does nearby development affect the value of my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: Generally no. Mineral rights and surface development are legally separate; production from an existing unit continues regardless of what's built above it elsewhere in the unit.

faqs.question: My lease is from the mid-2000s. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: Older leases can carry different deduction and royalty terms than newer ones. We review the specific language in your lease before making an offer.

faqs.question: What documents do you need from me to start?
faqs.answer: A copy of your deed or lease if you have one, and a recent royalty statement if you're currently receiving payments. We can locate anything missing through the county recorder.
